items.title: Lawrence "Buddy" Tureaud Interview, 1972-03-06
items.q: There was a man named Monette. Monette, he was the secretary.

ctx.x: Oh, well, well when, when you found out that the treasurer had, what had he done? He'd taken them, a. One. One. One. One. One. One. One. One. One.

There was a man named Monette. Monette, he was the secretary. Well, he used to collect money on the outside, and he'd go to the minor games, and take that money, and play minor, and with the time of the meeting come, he couldn't pay them people's money. What's a minor game, then? It was cards. You guessed the cards. You guessed them, you see? You guessed them, you pull them, you see? You put your money down on a card on the table, and if they pull that card, with your money on it, you win it. But if they don't…

Now that looks like it's working fine. I think the little needles are moving. It's moving. Well, yeah, it's moving. It's moving. It has even up. I haven't done this very much. I get nervous about it. I wanted to ask you about the Green O. I know I've seen the Green O over there on North Claiborne Avenue in St. Philip. Oh, yeah. But it's not a bar now. It's a liquor store. It's just a liquor store. But it used to be a bar. No, never did. No? I thought it was at one time. No. Well, did you run it? Yes. But it was…
